models.title: Ringdoku · 4 × 4
models.rule: Use 1–4 once in each ring, each spoke and each outlined curved region.
models.idea: The familiar starting point. Fewer givens can change the deduction sequence without increasing the symbol set.

models.title: Ringdoku · 6 × 6
models.rule: Use 1–6 once in each ring, each spoke and each outlined curved region.
models.idea: 36 cells and 1–6. More crossing groups; the six radial layers reduce the space for notes.

models.title: Ringdoku · 8 × 8
models.rule: Use 1–8 once in each ring, each spoke and each outlined curved region.
models.idea: 64 cells and 1–8. A useful density stress test; the inner ring notes become very small on a phone.

models.title: Wide rings · 1–6
models.rule: Use 1–6 once in each ring and each two-spoke wedge. An individual spoke has three cells and is not a separate 1–6 group.
models.idea: Three wider radial layers keep the cells larger. The changed group structure has more interchangeable positions, so unique puzzles need more givens.

models.title: Wide rings · 1–8
models.rule: Use 1–8 once in each ring and each two-spoke wedge. An individual spoke has four cells and is not a separate 1–8 group.
models.idea: Eight symbols without eight thin radial layers. It trades some crossing constraints for roomier cells.

models.title: Two independent 1–4 halves
models.rule: Each half is its own 1–4 Ringdoku: half-rings, spokes and curved regions use 1–4 once. No group crosses the divider.
models.idea: Exactly the two-simple-puzzles idea: more cells to fill, but two independent constraint components.

models.title: Linked halves · 1–4
models.rule: Use 1–4 once in each half-ring, spoke, curved region and selected bridge band. Bridge bands cross the two seams; tap a Bridge group to inspect it.
models.idea: The halves exchange information through bridge bands. Keep four candidate slots while adding interlocking deductions.

models.title: Three linked sections · 1–4
models.rule: Each third uses 1–4 in its ring segments, spokes and curved regions. Four-cell bridge bands cross all three seams.
models.idea: A mandala-like 48-cell option. Four note slots stay manageable; inner angular slices still need a phone-width check.

models.title: Venndoku · three circles / 1–6
models.rule: Each large circle contains 1–6 once. A cell belongs to every shape containing its center.
models.idea: The original overlap structure, now with varied uniquely solvable clue masks.

models.title: Venndoku · three circles / 1–8
models.rule: Each large circle contains 1–8 once. A cell belongs to every shape containing its center.
models.idea: Five exclusive cells per circle add capacity, but four of each five must be given to avoid interchangeable blank positions.

models.title: Four-circle clover · 1–4
models.rule: Each of the four large circles contains 1–4 once. The center belongs to all four circles.
models.idea: One exclusive cell per circle; extra shared groups rather than extra symbols.

models.title: Four-circle mesh · 1–6
models.rule: Each large circle contains 1–6 once. Some cells belong to three circles. The central all-four area has no cell.
models.idea: Twelve highly shared cells. Stronger coupling without filling the board with exclusive cells; triple intersections can be visually tight.

models.title: Five-petal mandala · 1–4
models.rule: Each petal circle contains 1–4 once. Neighboring petals share a cell, and the center belongs to all five.
models.idea: Eleven cells, five overlapping groups and four candidate slots. Explore more interlock before increasing the symbol range.

models.title: Three ovals · 1–6
models.rule: Each large oval contains 1–6 once. Shared cells count in every containing oval.
models.idea: Same memberships as the three-circle model. Changing the outline alone does not create a harder logical puzzle.

models.title: Three triangles · 1–6
models.rule: Each large triangle contains 1–6 once. Shared cells count in every triangle containing their center.
models.idea: Same group structure as the three-circle example. Pointed boundaries make some intersections narrower; this is a geometry comparison, not a new difficulty tier.
